Account snapshot: enterprise fintech company exploring Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for regulated trading-support and customer chat. Primary evaluation theme: deterministic throughput + predictable latency under bursty market events. Interested in reserved GPU planning with autoscale guarantees (warm pools) rather than pure on-demand.

Recent timeline & activities:
- 2026-01-12: Intro call (AE Sanjay) — high-level requirements, finance threshold flagged (~$300k ARR+). CTO (R. Kline) emphasized "no surprise tails" on latency.
- 2026-01-26: Technical deep-dive with SE (Ava) — discussed baseline throughput targets: 50k tokens/sec sustained for batch embedding jobs; interactive chat p95 < 200ms for 4k-token prompts (internal targets).
- 2026-02-03: Fireflies meeting ff_20260218_3872 — covered autoscaling mechanics, warm-pool concept, cold-start costs; asked for warmed-GPU pricing model.
- 2026-02-18: POC kickoff — Redwood shipped a staging cluster with 8xA100-equivalent reservations and autoscaler enabled. Baseline tests run against synthetic burst traces (market open spikes).
- 2026-02-25: Observability review (ff_20260225_3921) — token-level cost breakdown, tail-latency incidents captured; LatticeWave requested queueing SLA for backpressure behavior.
- 2026-03-03: Security Q&A submitted (drive:/security/LW_security_answers_2026.xlsx).

Use-case / Requirements summary (from calls & SE notes):
- Workloads: mixed interactive chat (low latency), high-throughput batch embeddings for nightly reindexes, and real-time reranking for alerts pipeline.
- SLOs: interactive p50 < 60ms, p95 < 200ms (4k prompt); streaming acceptable but must not exceed 350ms head-of-line p95 under bursts. Batch jobs: throughput committed in tokens/sec and embeddings/sec with windowed SLAs (e.g., 2M embeddings/hour).
- Throughput guarantees: want a committed baseline for peak 30-minute windows (market open/close). Expect Redwood to provision reserved GPUs to meet 95% of burst demand without cold-starts.
- Autoscaling & capacity management expectations:
  * Warm pools: pre-warmed GPU instances maintained during predictable windows (market hours) and for canary traffic. LatticeWave prefers configurable warm-pool sizing + pay-for-reservation model.
  * Scale-up policy: aggressive horizontal scale (~+50% nodes) when queue depth > X or avg token backlog > Y; policy needs confidence bounds to avoid oscillation in high-frequency bursts.
  * Scale-down policy: conservative cooldown (10-15 min) for interactive pools, longer for batch; warm-pool fallback to avoid cold-starts.
  * Queueing behavior: priority queues for interactive vs batch; backpressure signals (429 vs queued-with-estimate) required. They asked for SLA-friendly queueing semantics so upstream systems can implement graceful degradation.
  * Pre-warming timeline: want 60–90s warm-up for GPU partitions before taking live traffic; desire metrics around warm-up progress.
- SLA negotiation points:
  * Uptime target: enterprise SLA 99.95% for dedicated capacity (regional).
  * Remedies: service credits for missed SLOs; explicit throughput crediting (e.g., failure during peak window reduces committed tokens for next billing period).
  * Latency warranties: include p95 targets per route with clear measurement windows and excluded maintenance windows.
  * Capacity ramp clauses: ability to escalate reserved capacity for major events (e.g., M&A, product launches) with defined lead times and capped ramp costs.

POC findings (SE summary):
- Warm pool reduces tail events by ~70% for interactive traces during synthetic spikes.
- Autoscaler PID-like controller with hysteresis reduced oscillations compared to naive CPU-util-threshold method. SE recommends exposing hysteresis knobs to LatticeWave ops team.
- Observed queueing: when capacity saturated, batch jobs need to be throttled at ingress; LatticeWave requested built-in priority token buckets.

Commercial & procurement notes:
- Finance sign-off pending (decision maker: VP Finance, review week of 2026-03-22).
- Legal has redlines on SLA around data residency and uptime credits; Redwood legal to propose final language.
- Forecast: likely Q2 close if SLA language and warm-pool pricing acceptable.

Quotes / snippets from stakeholders:
- CTO (R. Kline): "We cannot have unpredictable tails at market open — that's where money is lost."
- Head of SRE: "Warm pools are non-negotiable during US market hours; we can compress batch windows overnight."

Next steps (short):
- Provide explicit warm-pool pricing options (3 sizes) and associated reserved-GPU commitment model (done by 2026-03-12).
- Legal to circulate SLA redline v1 (Redwood).
- Deploy autoscaler variant B in staging for live traffic replay (Ava to run, target 2026-03-15).
